answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the voyage schedule in the willow ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the vertex checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 5 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 96 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden genuine members do not face at scale. That is 3 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
